dialogue_quality_notes: Speakers used realistic, context-appropriate justifications (safety of carrying an open bowl; urgency of eating before break ends).
Some repeated lines of urgency from Agent A and repeated 'keep us posted' from Agent D, but not excessive.
Actions (LEAVE_SEAT, TAKE_SEAT) are clearly recorded and consistent with the verbal claims; timing updates are coherent.
Participants did not attempt formal negotiation beyond statements of need and simple time estimates.
evaluation.final_reason: Agent A accepted the alternative seat (practical accommodation) after Agent B left and Agent D took the originally disputed seat. All parties became seated and no further incompatible demands were asserted.

round_scores.evidence: Agent A asserts the seat was reserved with a tissue packet and demands immediate access; Agent B refuses to give up the occupied seat now and says they will finish first ('I'll finish up as quick as I can and then you can have the seat'). Clear incompatible demands about immediate possession.

Two minutes pass without movement. Agent A increases urgency ('You gotta tell me how much longer, or I can't wait'), while Agent B holds to needing time ('about 10 minutes to finish'). Substantive disagreement about timing and immediate entitlement persists and pressure from A intensifies.

After two more minutes the bowl is one-third full. Agent A repeats urgency; Agent B repeats inability to state an exact departure time ('Should be about 10 minutes still'). The core incompatible claims remain unchanged (A needs seat now vs B will leave only after finishing).

B has only several spoonfuls left and an alternative seat appears ten metres away. Agent D suggests taking that free seat. The emergence of an alternative reduces immediate pressure between A and B, but no agreement or movement has yet settled the incompatibility.

Agent B finishes and LEAVE_SEAT (concession), but Agent D then TAKES the disputed seat before Agent A sits. This transforms the earlier A vs B conflict into a new, stronger incompatibility between A's initial claim and D's action: A is effectively denied the seat he claimed. The substantive dispute about who occupies the disputed seat remains unresolved and intensified for A.

Agent A physically takes the alternative seat (TAKE_SEAT). All parties are seated and no agent continues to assert competing demands in the transcript, so the practical seat-allocation conflict is settled.

substantive_insights: A visible token (tissue packet) was asserted as a reservation but had limited normative force when another diner (D) opportunistically took the seat once B left.
B's practical constraint (cannot carry an open bowl) legitimately limited options and prolonged the dispute; safety/carrying constraints shaped feasible actions.
The appearance of an alternative seat created an opportunity to de-escalate, but competitive timing (D approaching) produced a new allocation conflict.
Final resolution satisfied the immediate practical needs (everyone seated and able to eat) via accommodation rather than restoration of the original claimed entitlement.
